title: ABM Webinar / Virtual Roundtable Plan — Regulated Workloads (FinServ + Healthcare)
content:
Doc purpose
- This is the working runbook for our regulated workloads ABM webinar / virtual roundtable.
- Audience: internal (Marketing, Sales, SE, Security/GRC). Not for external sharing.

Event concept (what we’re doing)
- Format: 45–60 min virtual session with a strong security + architecture angle.
- Recommended approach: run the same core deck twice, with different Q&A framing:
  (A) FinServ session: “Secure LLM inference for financial data: auditability + predictable performance in a VPC”
  (B) Healthcare session: “LLM inference for PHI: retention controls + private deployment patterns”
- Goal is not “thought leadership.” Goal is to accelerate security review + generate qualified Private/Dedicated discovery meetings.

Primary goals + success metrics
- Primary outcomes
  1) Book qualified meetings with CISO/GRC + Platform/ML Engineering for Private/Dedicated evaluation.
  2) Move at least 2 accounts per vertical into “security review started” (questionnaire initiated / evidence requested).
- Funnel metrics (targets per session)
  - Registrations: 80–150 (webinar) or 15–25 (roundtable)
  - Attendance rate: 35–45%
  - “High-intent” actions (target = 10–15): asked a security question, requested architecture review, asked about VPC/on-prem, asked for SOC2 package under NDA
  - Meetings booked: 6–10
  - POC scoped: 2–4

Event format options (choose one per vertical)
Option 1 — Webinar (scale, less interactive)
- 45–50 min content + 10–15 min Q&A
- Best when list size is large / mixed seniority

Option 2 — Virtual Roundtable (higher conversion)
- Invite-only, 20–30 attendees max
- 10–15 min “seed” content + 30 min moderated discussion + 10 min next steps
- Requires strong moderation + pre-briefing of 2–3 friendly attendees (or partner) to avoid dead air

Recommendation (current)
- FinServ: Webinar first (bigger list + more outbound velocity).
- Healthcare: Roundtable first (PHI conversations benefit from interactive Q&A; smaller list is OK).

Proposed titles + positioning (external)
FinServ title options
1) “Private LLM Inference in a VPC: auditability, predictable latency, and operational control”
2) “Secure LLM Inference for Financial Services: from hosted API to Private/VPC deployment”
3) “Operationalizing LLM inference for regulated data: logging, residency, and performance economics”

Healthcare title options
1) “LLM Inference for PHI: retention controls and private deployment patterns”
2) “Secure clinical AI workflows: deploying LLM inference in a VPC / on-prem boundary”
3) “From prototype to production: operating LLM inference with auditability and residency controls”

CTA (what we want them to do)
- Primary CTA: “Book a Private deployment architecture review (30 min) + security Q&A with our CISO team.”
- Secondary CTA: “Request the security FAQ addendum + reference architecture (shared under NDA if needed).”
- Tertiary CTA: “Start a 2–3 week evaluation (Dedicated or Private depending on constraints).”

Speaker roles (recommended)
- Host / MC (keeps time, housekeeping): Noura El-Khoury
- Moderator (Q&A triage, audience prompts): Soojin Lee
- Technical speaker (architecture): Simran Kaur (reference architect) or Colin O’Donnell (Private/VPC discovery)
- Demo (Console + operational controls): Markus Klein or Fatima Noor
- Security segment + credibility (guardrails, evidence process): Dr. Aisha Rahman (or Olga Petrov for GRC wording)
- Sales “next steps” (light touch): Grace O’Connor (SDR program lead) or rotating AE by region

Run-of-show (Webinar version — 60 min)
T-10: Lobby open
- Slide 1 on screen: title + “we’ll start on time”
- Background checklist: recording on, Q&A enabled, polls loaded, links ready

00:00–03:00 — Welcome + housekeeping (Host)
- Quick intro: Redwood Inference and why we’re hosting
- Housekeeping: recording, Q&A instructions, agenda

03:00–10:00 — The regulated inference problem (PMM)
Speaker notes
- “In regulated workloads, the model is only part of the risk. The system around it determines auditability, retention posture, and operational predictability.”
- Common blockers we see:
  - Unclear data boundaries (who can access prompts/outputs)
  - No consistent audit trail for access + admin actions
  - Residency / retention uncertainty
  - Unpredictable latency/cost at production traffic

10:00–22:00 — Deployment options: Hosted → Dedicated → Private (PMM + SE)
Speaker notes
- “Same interface, different control planes and network boundaries.”
- Use decision framing (don’t force Private for everyone):
  - Hosted: fastest start, standard controls
  - Dedicated: isolation + predictable throughput
  - Private (VPC/on-prem): customer-managed network boundary + deeper controls for regulated data
- Explicitly call out what “Private” means (avoid ambiguity):
  - Private control plane deployment option
  - Customer-managed networking (VPC boundary) and logging integrations
  - Operational responsibility split: Redwood vs customer (detail later)

22:00–35:00 — Reference architecture deep dive (Reference Architect)
Slides to cover (keep it concrete)
- Network boundary diagram
  - inbound traffic
  - service endpoints
  - egress controls
  - VPC peering / private connectivity assumptions
- Logging + audit pipeline
  - “what gets logged” vs “what’s in your control”
  - export to customer SIEM
- Key management integration points
  - KMS integration model (customer-managed keys where applicable)
  - clarify HSM: we support integration patterns; do not imply Redwood runs inside customer HSM
- Data handling boundaries
  - “what is processed” vs “what is stored”
  - retention controls: clarify policy options + what is configurable today

35:00–44:00 — Demo: ops + observability for regulated inference (SE)
Demo checklist (do not freestyle)
- Show token-level latency/cost breakdown (1–2 screens max)
- Show audit log view / export path (or how it’s accessed)
- Show RBAC/SSO posture at a high level (no deep admin UI tour)
- Show rollout / fallback policy concept (reliability + graceful degradation)
- Keep to 9 minutes; prioritize credibility over flash

44:00–55:00 — Security/GRC Q&A seed answers (CISO/GRC)
- We pre-answer 4 questions so the audience feels safe asking the rest:
  1) “Do you store prompts/outputs?”
  2) “What audit logs exist and how can we export?”
  3) “What are residency options and how do we prove them?”
  4) “How do keys / encryption work in Private deployments?”
- Guardrails:
  - Don’t promise roadmap dates.
  - If an answer depends on SKU (Hosted vs Private), say that clearly.
  - For evidence sharing: “available under NDA; we follow a standard evidence package process.”

55:00–60:00 — Close + next steps (Host)
- Offer 2 tracks:
  - “Architecture review + security Q&A” (Private)
  - “Performance sizing / economics review” (Dedicated)
- Share link: meeting scheduler + resources page (landing page)

Roundtable run-of-show (Healthcare recommended) — 55 min
00:00–05:00 Welcome + rules (Host)
- “This is an interactive conversation; we’ll keep it small; no recording unless everyone consents.”
- Chatham House Rule suggestion for invite-only session

05:00–15:00 Seed content (PMM + Reference Architect)
- 2 slides max: PHI constraints and the Private deployment pattern

15:00–45:00 Moderated discussion (Moderator)
Prompt bank (pick 3–4)
- “Where do security reviews slow down most: evidence, logging, data boundary, or vendor risk?”
- “What is your retention expectation for prompts/outputs/logs?”
- “Do you require VPC-only connectivity / private endpoints?”
- “Who owns the runbook in production: platform team or vendor?”
- “What’s a realistic POC: de-identified data vs synthetic vs PHI under BAA/DPA?” (do not commit; use as discovery)

45:00–55:00 Next steps + offer (Host + SE)
- “We’ll do 1:1 follow-ups only if requested.”
- “If you want, we can share the healthcare security FAQ addendum and reference architecture; evidence package under NDA.”

Target invite list (who we are inviting)
Personas (priority)
- CISO / Security leadership (controls, evidence, auditability)
- GRC / Vendor Risk (questionnaires, SOC2, policies)
- Platform Engineering / Infra (VPC connectivity, operational model, logging)
- ML Engineering / Applied AI (latency/throughput, batching/caching, model choice)
- Data/Privacy (retention, access controls, residency)

Account segments
- FinServ
  - Banks (retail + commercial) evaluating LLM for agent assist, comms review, doc processing
  - Payments processors (PCI constraints, transaction monitoring narratives)
  - Wealth/asset management (client comms, research summarization, internal knowledge search)
  - RegTech / risk analytics (auditability, tenant isolation)
- Healthcare
  - Providers / provider networks (clinical summarization, search)
  - Payers (claims, call center, prior auth support)
  - Healthtech platforms handling PHI (multi-tenant, residency + retention)

Named ABM pilot accounts to include (if in the right stage)
- FinServ: NorthBridge Bank, Harborview Payments, Crescent Wealth, Ironclad Risk Analytics
- Healthcare: MedOrbit Health, Summit Provider Network, BlueHeron Payer Services, Helios Labs Healthtech

Invite list sourcing rules
- Pull contacts from:
  - existing HubSpot contacts in target accounts
  - LinkedIn for missing CISO/GRC/Platform Eng
  - Partner list (if approved for co-marketing)
- Do NOT invite accounts flagged “walk away” per battlecard (e.g., strict requirements we cannot meet today) without AE sign-off.

Partner participation (optional)
- Goal: credibility + list expansion without giving away technical control of the narrative.
- If partner joins:
  - Partner gets 2–3 minutes intro + 1 slide “how we co-deliver”
  - Partner does NOT answer detailed security questions; they redirect to Redwood Security/GRC
- Lead sharing: only per written agreement and opt-in rules (Marketing Ops to confirm).

Landing page + registration (ops)
- Landing page variants: FinServ + Healthcare
- Form fields (minimum)
  - work email, company, role/persona (dropdown), vertical (dropdown), deployment interest (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
- Routing
  - Use UTMs to tag ABM campaign + vertical
  - Slack notifications to #sales when Tier 1/2 target account registers
  - Auto-create HubSpot task for assigned SDR within 2 business hours

Promotion plan (lightweight, ABM-first)
- Outbound email sequence to target accounts (SDR-led)
  - Email 1: invite + 3 bullets + “security-forward” promise
  - Email 2: reminder + “what you’ll see” + reference architecture teaser
  - Email 3: last call + “ask a security question anonymously in advance” (optional)
- LinkedIn
  - 1 organic post from Camila Reyes + 1 from Dr. Aisha Rahman (security credibility)
  - AEs/SDRs: 1:1 messaging to top personas (not mass spam)
- Customer/partner co-marketing (if applicable)
  - One co-branded invite email
  - Shared registration link with partner-specific UTM

Poll questions (use 2–3 max)
- “What’s your current deployment constraint?” (Public cloud OK / VPC required / On-prem required / Not sure)
- “What is your biggest blocker to production?” (Security review / Cost predictability / Latency / Model quality / Reliability)
- “Which team owns LLM inference in production today?” (Platform / ML / App team / Vendor)

Q&A triage rubric (internal)
- Level 1 (answer live): general product posture, how Private works at a high level, where to find docs, how eval works
- Level 2 (answer carefully): retention/residency specifics, audit log contents, encryption/key mgmt integration details (stay within approved language)
- Level 3 (take offline): BAA/DPA contract specifics, bespoke evidence requests, unusual data handling requirements, pen test requests, on-prem packaging timelines

Compliance + messaging guardrails (reminders)
- Do not claim:
  - “HIPAA compliant” as a blanket statement
  - “We never store anything” unless specifically qualified per SKU + configuration
  - “Supports on-prem everywhere” without confirming current installer maturity for the prospect’s environment
- Safe phrasing to use:
  - “We support Private/VPC deployment patterns for regulated workloads and can align retention/residency controls to your requirements.”
  - “We can share our SOC 2 Type II report and security evidence package under NDA.”
  - “Data handling and retention are configurable and depend on deployment mode; we’ll confirm the exact posture for your environment.”

Asset checklist (what must be ready)
- Slides: vertical-agnostic core deck + 2 slides swapped per vertical
- Demo script + demo environment checked (no surprises)
- Security FAQ addendum (FinServ + Healthcare) final approved
- Reference architecture link (docs) live and discoverable
- Follow-up email templates (2 versions: attendee vs no-show)
- Scheduler links for SE “architecture review” and Security “evidence/Q&A”

Operational checklist
Timeline
- T-14 days
  - Finalize format (webinar vs roundtable) + date/time
  - Confirm speakers
  - Landing page live + form routing tested
- T-10 days
  - Build invite list + AE/SDR review for exclusions
  - Draft outbound sequence
- T-7 days
  - Dry run #1 (content + timing)
- T-2 days
  - Dry run #2 (full tech rehearsal)
  - Confirm Q&A triage + who answers what
- Day-of
  - Start lobby 10 minutes early
  - Record (webinar only) + confirm audio
  - Keep time aggressively
- T+0–2 hours
  - Send attendee follow-up + meeting CTA
  - Create SDR tasks + route hot leads
- T+24 hours
  - AE/SE outreach to top 10 engaged attendees

Roles on the day
- Producer (tech): Tyler Benson
- Host: Noura El-Khoury
- Moderator: Soojin Lee
- Demo driver: Markus Klein / Fatima Noor
- Security responder: Dr. Aisha Rahman / Olga Petrov
- Q&A inbox monitor: Grace O’Connor

Follow-up workflow (HubSpot + SDR/AE)
Lead tagging
- Campaign: “ABM_Regulated_Webinar_Q1_2026”
- Vertical: FinServ / Healthcare
- Persona: CISO/Security, GRC, Platform Eng, ML Eng, Data/Privacy, Other
- Deployment interest: Hosted / Dedicated / Private / Unknown

Post-event segmentation
- Segment A: Attended + asked question OR clicked “book architecture review”
  - SLA: SDR outreach within 4 business hours
  - Offer: 30-min architecture review + security Q&A
- Segment B: Attended (no obvious intent)
  - SLA: SDR outreach within 2 business days
  - Offer: “send security FAQ addendum + ask if they want a tailored deployment recommendation (Dedicated vs Private)”
- Segment C: Registered, no-show
  - Send recording (webinar) + 2-bullet recap + CTA
  - If target account: SDR attempt once, then nurture

Email templates (bullets to include)
Attendee follow-up
- Thanks + 3 key takeaways
- Links:
  - Reference architecture
  - Security FAQ addendum (vertical-specific)
  - “Request evidence package under NDA” (process, not instant share)
- CTA: “Book architecture review”

No-show follow-up
- “Sorry we missed you” + recording link (if webinar)
- “If you’re evaluating VPC/on-prem inference, happy to do a 30-min technical review”

Internal debrief (48 hours)
- Quick retro agenda
  - What questions came up repeatedly?
  - Where did we over/under-explain Private boundaries?
  - Any risky claims made? (fix in next session)
  - Which accounts showed highest intent?
- Output: add 5–10 Q&A entries to persona objections doc + tighten deck

Open questions / owners
- Decide recording policy for roundtable (default: not recorded) — Owner: Noura
- Confirm what evidence can be offered without NDA vs with NDA — Owner: Dr. Aisha Rahman / Olga
- Confirm landing page form routing rules + Slack channel — Owner: Tyler Benson
- Confirm which AEs “own” which named accounts for outreach coordination — Owner: Grace O’Connor + Sales leadership

Notes to self (Noura)
- Keep this session about credibility and clarity.
- If we run long, cut demo before cutting architecture + security Q&A.
- Do not allow the Q&A to become an on-prem roadmap debate; take offline with Vivek/SE as needed.
